general_conventions: B marks are independent marks awarded only when the specific point is seen in the answer.
M marks are method marks; if an M mark is not scored, the A marks that depend on it cannot be scored.
C marks are compensatory method marks: they can be awarded even if the equation/step is not written, provided later correct working shows it was known.
A marks are accuracy/answer marks that depend on an M mark or allow C marks to be scored; A0 in a 'show that' means the given value earns no mark itself.
ECF (error carried forward): a wrong earlier answer used correctly later is not penalised again.
AW = alternative wording accepted; ORA = or reverse argument; '/' separates alternative acceptable answers; words in brackets are not essential; underlined words must be present.
'reject'/'not' = answers not worthy of credit; 'ignore' = irrelevant statements that neither gain nor lose credit; 'allow' = acceptable answers.

Annotations used include BOD (benefit of doubt), CON (contradiction), ECF, L1/L2/L3 (levels), TE (transcription error), POT (power-of-ten error), SF (significant figure error), WP (wrong physics or equation).
Significant figures: if data are given to 2 s.f., answers to 2 or more s.f. are allowed; an answer to fewer than 2 s.f. is penalised once only in the whole paper unless guidance says otherwise.

Level of Response (6-mark, asterisked) questions: examiner first decides the level (L1 1-2, L2 3-4, L3 5-6) from the science content against the descriptor, then the mark within the level from the quality of communication/line of reasoning; indicative points are guidance, not a checklist; 0 for no response worthy of credit.
Alternative correct answers and unexpected approaches must be credited fairly.
Additional RM Assessor annotations in this series include follow through, not answered question, rounding/repeated error and arithmetic error.

questions.context: Define stopping distance of a vehicle.
marking_points: B1: sum of thinking distance and braking distance
allow_reject_ignore: Allow total distance travelled from seeing a hazard until the vehicle stops

questions.context: Convert 61 km h^-1 to about 17 m s^-1.
Initial KE of a 1.9 × 10^5 kg train.
Average deceleration stopping in 310 m.
Average braking force on the train.
Compare stopping distance on an incline with level track, same braking force.
questions.answer: Shorter: weight component acts down slope with braking force (some KE → GPE), larger net decelerating force.
marking_points: B1: weight component acts down incline/same direction as braking force (or some KE transferred to GPE)
B1: smaller distance as larger net opposing force / greater deceleration / less work by brakes
pitfalls: Vague reference to gravity without component

questions.context: Complete extension column for spring data.
marking_points: B1: column heading and all extension values correct

questions.context: Plot e against F and draw best-fit line.
questions.answer: Labelled axes, sensible scale, accurate points, ruled best-fit line.
marking_points: B1: y-axis labelled e/cm
B1: simple y scale using at least half the grid
B1: points plotted correctly (checked at (0.98,1.8) and (2.45,4.6)), blobs < half small square
B1: straight best-fit line drawn with ruler
allow_reject_ignore: Tick labels at least every 2 large squares
pitfalls: Using less than half the paper

questions.context: Gradient of best-fit line.
marking_points: B1: gradient in range 1.80–1.94 (or 0.0180–0.0194)
pitfalls: Using a small triangle or data points off the line

questions.context: Force constant of two-spring combination from gradient, with unit.
marking_points: C1: k2 = 1/gradient
A1: correct value with unit N cm^-1 or N m^-1 to 2 or 3 s.f.
allow_reject_ignore: Unit must match power of ten
pitfalls: Taking k = gradient (graph is e vs F)

questions.context: Whether the graph shows Hooke's law is obeyed.
questions.answer: Hooke's law: extension ∝ force; conclusion depends on whether the line is straight through origin.
marking_points: B1: extension directly proportional to load (within elastic limit)
B1: graph is (or isn't) a straight line through the origin so law is (not) obeyed

questions.context: Ratio of force constants for three versus two identical springs in series.
marking_points: C1: k1 = 2k2 or series rule k/n

questions.context: How to measure a sphere's diameter precisely.
questions.answer: Micrometer/vernier calipers; repeat in different orientations and average.
marking_points: B1: micrometer or vernier caliper
B1: repeat readings (in different directions) and average

questions.subtopic: density and volume of a sphere
questions.context: Show mass of wooden sphere from density and diameter.
allow_reject_ignore: Allow 4/3π(1.4)³ in cm³ for first M

questions.context: Force needed to hold sphere fully submerged and stationary in water.
pitfalls: Forgetting weight acts with the applied force

questions.context: Describe a safe experiment (with diagram) to test v = Kr² for spheres in a liquid and find K.
questions.answer: Drop spheres of measured radii in long tube; time over marked intervals to confirm terminal velocity; plot v vs r², K = gradient.
marking_points: L3 (5-6): clear procedure, measurements and analysis; well-developed logical reasoning
L2 (3-4): some procedure, some measurements and some analysis
L1 (1-2): limited procedure and limited measurements or limited analysis
0: nothing creditworthy

Procedure: labelled diagram; long tube; method to find terminal velocity and to check it is reached (equal times over equal distances); safety (tray for spills, gloves, clamp tube); method to retrieve sphere
Measurements: diameter by micrometer/caliper, averaged; distance and time (stopwatch, ruler, light gates with timer, video analysis); repeat for each r
Analysis: r = d/2; calculate v = distance/time; plot v against r²; K = gradient (straight line through origin)
pitfalls: Not checking terminal velocity is reached before timing
Plotting v against r rather than r²

questions.context: Show heater element resistance ≈ 15 Ω from rated power and voltage.
marking_points: A0

questions.context: Length of heater wire from resistivity, radius and resistance.
Whether the heater element obeys Ohm's law.
questions.answer: No: Ohm's law needs constant temperature; element heats so resistance changes.
marking_points: B1: V ∝ I provided physical conditions (temperature) constant
B1: temperature not constant so Ohm's law not obeyed
allow_reject_ignore: Allow one mark for 'not obeyed because resistance changes as temperature changes'
pitfalls: Defining Ohm's law as V = IR only

questions.context: Weekly cost of running three heaters 7 hours each night at a given price per kWh.
marking_points: C1: energy = 3 × 3.5 × 7 × 7 = 514.5 kWh (any correct partial product)
pitfalls: Miscounting hours (midnight to 7 am is 7 h)

questions.context: Voltmeter reading across fixed resistor with thermistor and variable resistor in series.
How voltmeter reading changes as thermistor temperature rises.
questions.answer: Thermistor resistance falls, total resistance falls/current rises, greater pd across fixed resistor, voltmeter reading increases.
marking_points: B1: thermistor resistance decreases as temperature increases
B1: total resistance decreases or current increases
M1: greater share of pd across fixed resistor
A1: voltmeter reading increases
pitfalls: Concluding without the pd-share reasoning (A depends on M)

questions.context: Define phase difference and coherence.
questions.answer: Phase difference: angular difference between points/waves; coherence: constant phase difference.
marking_points: B1: phase difference - difference in angle (degrees/radians) between points on a wave or similar points on two waves
B1: coherence - constant phase difference
allow_reject_ignore: Must compare points/waves; allow 'how far out of step'

questions.context: Explain bright line at P and dark line at Q via path difference.
questions.answer: P: path difference nλ (constructive); Q: path difference (n+½)λ (destructive).
marking_points: B1: P - path difference is a whole number of wavelengths (constructive)
B1: Q - path difference is an odd number of half wavelengths (destructive)
allow_reject_ignore: Allow nλ or λ; not phase difference
pitfalls: Using phase difference instead of path difference

questions.context: Wavelength from measured fringe pattern width, slit separation and screen distance.
marking_points: C1: fringe separation x = 4.22 mm (42.2 mm across 10 spacings)

questions.context: Percentage uncertainty in wavelength from uncertainties in D, a and pattern width.
marking_points: C1: any one fractional uncertainty (0.02/4.5, 0.02/0.56, 0.2/42.2)
Alt: B1 λmax or λmin calculated; B1 Δλ/λ × 100 ≈ 4.4 or 4.6 %
pitfalls: Multiplying or averaging uncertainties instead of adding percentages

questions.context: Photons emitted per second by 50.0 mW laser.
marking_points: C1: photon energy = hc/λ = 3.79 × 10^-19 J

questions.context: Whether green light causes emission from metal of work function 2.6 eV.
questions.answer: No: photon energy (≈2.4 eV) less than work function (4.16 × 10^-19 J).
marking_points: M1: convert 2.6 eV = 4.16 × 10^-19 J (or photon energy 2.37 eV)
A1: photon energy less than work function so no emission

questions.context: Difference between stationary and progressive waves.
questions.answer: Progressive transfers energy, same amplitude everywhere; stationary no net energy transfer, nodes/antinodes, varying amplitude.
marking_points: B1: progressive wave transfers energy / all points same amplitude
B1: stationary wave no net energy transfer / has nodes with zero amplitude / amplitude varies
allow_reject_ignore: Stationary has nodes and antinodes alone = 1 mark

questions.subtopic: resonance in closed and open tubes
questions.context: Explain resonant frequencies in a closed and open tube; describe determining speed of sound.
questions.answer: Closed: node at closed end, antinode open end, L = λ/4, odd harmonics; open: antinodes both ends, L = λ/2, all harmonics; v = fλ ≈ 338 m s^-1.
marking_points: L3 (5-6): clear explanation of observations and correct method for speed of sound; well-developed logical reasoning
L2 (3-4): clear explanation or correct method, or limited explanation and limited method
L1 (1-2): limited explanation or limited method
0: nothing creditworthy

Explanation: stationary wave from interference of incident and reflected waves; nodes and antinodes; node at closed end, antinode at open end; longitudinal oscillation direction of air; fundamental for closed (λ/4 = L, 130 Hz) and open (λ/2 = L, 260 Hz); harmonics for closed tube (odd multiples) and open tube (all multiples)
Speed of sound: correct λ–L link; v = fλ; v calculated for different harmonics/tubes or graphical method; ≈338 m s^-1
pitfalls: Ignoring the odd-only harmonics of closed tube
